questions.q: In 'The Stag, the Sheep, and the Wolf', what did the Stag ask the Sheep to lend him?
choices: A measure of wheat
Some of her wool
A bag of gold coins
A warm blanket
questions.evidence: lend him a measure of wheat

questions.q: In 'The Stag, the Sheep, and the Wolf', why did the Sheep refuse to trust the Stag?
choices: The Wolf never pays, and the Stag could run away
The Stag had been rude to her the week before
She had no wheat left in her barn to lend him
The Stag was too young to borrow from anyone
questions.evidence: He takes what he wants and runs off with it without paying.

questions.q: In 'The Animals and the Plague', why did the Lion call a council?
choices: To find the most guilty animal to sacrifice
To choose which animal should be the next king
To plan a big feast for all the forest animals
To get the animals ready to fight the shepherds
questions.evidence: the most guilty one of us must be offered in sacrifice

questions.q: In 'The Animals and the Plague', what did the Fox say about the Lion eating sheep?
choices: That it was no crime and even an honor to the sheep
That it was a terrible sin that brought the plague
That the Lion should be punished like the rest of them
That the sheep tasted bad and were not worth eating
questions.evidence: Can it be a crime to eat sheep

questions.q: In 'The Animals and the Plague', what did the Ass confess to doing?
choices: Nibbling a bit of grass from the priests' field
Eating a shepherd who came into the woods
Stealing a fat lamb from the farmer's fold at night
Biting the Lion's tail while he was asleep
questions.evidence: I could not resist nibbling a bit of it

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Animals and the Plague'?
choices: The weak are made to suffer for the misdeeds of the powerful
Always tell the whole truth, even when you are very afraid
Grass from a priest's field is bad for an Ass to eat
Lions are always fair rulers who treat every animal the same
questions.evidence: The weak are made to suffer for the misdeeds of the powerful.

questions.q: In 'The Shepherd and the Lion', what did the Shepherd promise Jupiter after he saw the Lion?
choices: A full-grown Bull if the thief would go away
A fat Calf if Jupiter would help find the thief
All of his Sheep if the Lion would spare him
A new temple built on the top of the hill
questions.evidence: Now I promise you a full-grown Bull, if you but make the thief go away!

questions.q: In 'The Shepherd and the Lion', why did the Shepherd no longer want to catch the thief?
choices: The thief was a huge Lion, much scarier than a Wolf
He had found his missing Sheep down by the river
He got tired of looking and wanted to go home
The Wolf came and said he was sorry for stealing
questions.evidence: a huge Lion stalked out, carrying a Sheep
